items.title: WordPress.org's Protect the Shire has blocked over 100 severe plugin releases since September
items.summary: WordPress.org's Plugins Team says its Protect the Shire initiative has automatically blocked more than 100 plugin releases with severe security issues since September. The latest were backdoored releases of six WP connect plugins on 22 Nov, which Wordfence rated 9.8 (critical).
items.why: The release hold is catching compromised plugin updates before they reach sites, but it does not cover plugins sold outside WordPress.org. Keep auto-updates for those under review and keep backups current.

items.title: Switzerland confirms AI-agent attacks breached four of five victims, including critical infrastructure
items.summary: Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre says AI agents broke into systems in four of five confirmed attacks, three of which targeted critical infrastructure operators. The UK NCSC and Italy's CSIRT report the same pattern, and Switzerland advises installing critical updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours of release.
items.why: The attacks use old weaknesses: unpatched software, default or missing authentication, exposed credentials. Patch client sites quickly and check that no keys or passwords sit in repositories.

items.title: Gutenberg 24.5 adds Grid placement, side-by-side style revisions and notes across blocks
items.summary: Gutenberg 24.5, released on 25 Nov, lets you place any block on a specific column and row of a Grid. It also shows style revisions side by side with current styles, and lets one note cover text across several blocks.
items.why: Useful for Gutenberg-based client sites where you want precise layouts without custom CSS. Try it on staging first.

items.title: Unpatched Cacti zero-day gives remote code execution in four requests via the guest account
items.summary: Details of an unpatched flaw in Cacti Core 1.2.31, the latest version, have been published with a proof of concept. An unauthenticated attacker using the default guest account can reach command execution as the Cacti server user. It has no CVE identifier yet.
items.why: Only matters if you or a client host Cacti. Until a fix ships, disable the guest account and restrict access to the web interface.

items.title: Nvidia tells partners to pause server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
items.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, Nvidia has told partners including Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks that regional partners meet US export requirements. Chinese firms had been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there.
items.why: Nothing to do, but it tightens AI compute supply and could affect cloud GPU availability and prices.

items.title: Google to publish Android developers' phone number and address under EU trader rules
items.summary: Developers have until 1 Feb 2027 to declare whether they are a trader under UK and EU law. Those who do will have contact details, including phone number and address, made public from 1 Mar 2027. Google does not accept PO boxes for the payment profile address.
items.why: Relevant only if you or a client publishes monetised Android apps on Google Play. Decide before 1 Feb whether to use a business address.

items.title: OpenAI fixes a billing bug, so GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage limits are reached faster
items.summary: OpenAI says a billing mistake incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage. After the fix, users reach limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week. OpenAI adds one banked usage reset for Go, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers.
items.why: If you use these models for coding, expect quotas to run out sooner. Check Settings > Usage and keep Claude as a fallback.

actions.title: Update every client site to WordPress 7.1.5
actions.detail: The release fixes 20 security issues, including an unauthenticated flaw that could lead to remote code execution.

actions.title: Ask hosts to update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or later
actions.detail: CVE-2026-125396 lets a crafted uploaded file run commands on servers that render uploads with Ghostscript.
